object_types.name: SpendTier

object_types.name: RiskTier
object_types.definition: Compliance's classification of a vendor by risk level, derived from the risk review.

object_types.name: RiskReview

ambiguities.description: Contact's own identification scheme is not stated. The transcript describes contacts as name/email/phone tied to vendor+region but never mentions a contact identifier (e.g., contact ID). Is Contact identified only by the Vendor+Region combination (making it effectively part of that relationship rather than an independent entity), or does it have its own ID?

source_references.excerpt: Each vendor has one primary contact. Name, email, phone number.
A given vendor in a given region has exactly one primary contact.

ambiguities.description: The exact mechanism/timing linking RiskReview 'current' status to Vendor active status is not fully specified as a formal constraint -- is 'active' status itself derived from having a current signed-off review, or are these independently maintained fields with a business rule enforced procedurally? The facilitator states it as a rule but Raj describes it as a system-enforced transition block, suggesting possible derivation.

source_references.excerpt: I've watched it happen. But the system does enforce it -- you cannot move a vendor to active without a completed review, the transition is blocked.
Every active vendor has a current signed-off risk review. Draft vendors have none.

ambiguities.description: What happens to in-flight Purchase Orders when a Vendor is suspended (e.g., a possible 'run-off' status) is explicitly unresolved and pending a steering group decision. No constraint should be modeled for post-suspension fulfilment yet.

source_references.excerpt: Parking it explicitly: what happens to in-flight purchase orders when a vendor is suspended is undecided.

ambiguities.description: The term 'tier' is overloaded: Dana's spend tier (bronze/silver/gold) and Raj's risk tier (low/medium/high) are both called 'tier' by stakeholders, causing confusion in conversation even though the system stores them as separate fields. Should the model/documentation enforce the 'spend tier' / 'risk tier' naming to avoid ambiguity in future discussions?

source_references.excerpt: And you both call it "tier." / We both call it tier and it causes genuine chaos.

ambiguities.description: Vendor addresses (remit-to, ship-from, legal) are mentioned as three distinct, frequently different values, but no structure or identification scheme was defined for them in this session. Should each address be modeled as a separate value type/fact type (e.g., Vendor has RemitToAddress) with its own structure (street, city, etc.), and is granularity of a single text field sufficient?

source_references.excerpt: Address, though we have three addresses really -- remit-to, ship-from, and the legal one, which are frequently different and frequently wrong.

ambiguities.description: Mei's informal spreadsheet (including the 'preferred vendor' flag) was explicitly declared out of scope / ad hoc and not to be modeled, per stakeholder agreement. No rule exists to capture this, but it represents an acknowledged gap in the system that may need governance in future sessions.

source_references.excerpt: I'm going to note that as a gap rather than a rule... / It's ad hoc. Don't model it.

ambiguities.description: Duplicate vendor records (same tax ID, same company onboarded twice) are a known, unresolved data quality issue explicitly out of scope for this session's model, but they affect the reliability of any Vendor-TaxId analysis and compliance aggregate exposure reporting.

source_references.excerpt: We have vendors with the same tax ID... / Noted, but out of scope for today. Tax ID isn't an identifier, vendor number is.
The duplicates are also a compliance problem, for what it's worth. If we've got the same entity twice we can't see aggregate exposure.

ambiguities.description: Whether RiskReview history (all past reviews) needs explicit temporal tracking beyond the 'current' flag is unclear -- the transcript mentions re-review cycles and that old reviews are never edited, implying a need to track review effective/expiry dates, but no such value type or constraint was specified.

source_references.excerpt: A vendor can have several reviews over its life -- we re-review on a cycle, and every re-review is a new record, we don't edit the old one.
